title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Ethan Cole
description: Motivation: several production workloads show model-specific regressions for Llama, Mistral and Qwen families due to quantization packing, attention tiling, and suboptimal kernel selection under GQA/MQA profiles. This PR introduces targeted runtime changes: 1) model-specific kernel selection rules and tuned GEMM tiling (LLAMA_ROTARY/ALPAKER variants), 2) attention kernel improvements for narrow-head Mistral variants to avoid excessive memory traffic, 3) KV cache compaction and pointer-aliasing to reduce memcpy when serving Qwen-style grouped KV layouts, and 4) GQA/MQA-aware dequant/drain paths that avoid unnecessary roundtrips between int8 and fp16 for small-batch/low-latency requests. The description below summarizes the work and operational impact. Changes: - New kernel selector: runtime/kernel_selector.rs adds heuristics to choose pack/unpack kernels based on model meta (head_dim, num_heads, rotary_frac) and live sequence-length distribution. Selector prefers fused pack-kernel for GQA when head_dim % 32 == 0, falls back to MQA-mapped kernels for mixed-precision models. - Llama attention: runtime/attention/llama_tiled.rs implements tiled attention with improved rotary indexing and a micro-batching path that preserves KV stride for long-prefix workloads; reduces p95 by ~18% on internal chat traces. - Mistral narrow-head tuning: runtime/attention/mistral_narrow.rs introduces a specialty kernel to avoid wide GEMM rounding that previously inflated memory bandwidth. - Qwen KV layout: runtime/kv_cache.rs now supports a compacted grouped-KV representation for Qwen GQA exports and introduces zero-copy aliasing for contiguous per-batch KV reads. - Continuous batching and scheduler: runtime/scheduler.rs updated to allow model-aware batching windows (shorter windows for GQA small-head models to maintain latency SLOs) and opportunistic micro-batches for steady throughput. - GQA/MQA quantization path: runtime/quantization/gqa_mqa.rs adds tuning parameters and a fast path that keeps compute in int8 when post-op stability allows, otherwise falls back to fp16 with minimal copies. - Tests & benchmarks: benchmarks/perf/{llama,mistral,qwen}_gqa_perf.py added model-specific benchmarks; tests/kv_compaction_test.rs and tests/kernel_selector_test.rs added. Impact: internal perf lab numbers show median latency reductions of 8-12% for Llama-family chat workloads, 10-20% for Mistral narrow-head configs, and 12-25% throughput uplift for high-concurrency Qwen GQA workloads with reduced GPU memory footprint (up to 15% less KV memory in long-context cases). Compatibility: runtime auto-detects model meta and only enables model-specific paths when metadata matches known signatures; fallback to previous generic kernels remains. Migration & Ops: rollout gated behind a Canary config (console rollout flag: runtime.model_optimizations.gqa_mqa); observability hooks added to emit kernel_selection and kv_compaction metrics (perf.kernel.selected, kv.compaction.enabled) to validate behavior in prod. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for selector + kv compaction - [x] Perf benchmarks in lab - [x] Canary rollout config + metrics - [x] Docs upgrade note in docs/upgrade-notes.md - [x] CI green on main branch

release_notes: Model-specific runtime optimizations for Llama/Mistral/Qwen that improve latency and throughput under GQA/MQA quantization.
KV cache compaction for Qwen reduces GPU KV memory footprint for long-context workloads.
New kernel selection heuristics and GQA/MQA fast paths (opt-in via runtime.model_optimizations.gqa_mqa canary).
operational_instructions: Enable runtime.model_optimizations.gqa_mqa=false in prod for initial rollout; monitor perf.kernel.selected and kv.compaction.enabled metrics.
Canary rollout plan: enable for 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% assuming no regression in p95 latency and error rates.
If p95 regresses, disable canary and revert via console flag. For emergency rollback, set runtime.model_optimizations.gqa_mqa=false and redeploy scheduler agents.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the serving team and perf lab; follow-up PRs planned for terraform toggles and docs examples for model metadata tagging.
